author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Jakob Ingebrigtsen withdrew from Sunday’s 1,500-meter race at the Ultimate Championship, postponing another anticipated meeting with British rival Josh Kerr. The Norwegian runner had won the 5,000 meters on Friday but decided against racing twice within three days as he continues his recovery from Achilles surgery.

Ingebrigtsen underwent the operation in February and returned to competition last month after nearly a year away. His Friday victory showed that he could again handle championship-level racing, but the shorter turnaround presented a different recovery demand. The withdrawal leaves the 1,500 without one of its highest-profile entrants.

The decision also delays a rivalry that has become one of middle-distance running’s central storylines. Ingebrigtsen and Kerr have not raced each other since 2024, and their tactical contrast makes each scheduled meeting a major event. For Ingebrigtsen, the choice prioritizes a controlled return over adding another race immediately after the 5,000. Kerr remains in the field, while the Norwegian’s next chance to test himself over 1,500 meters will depend on his recovery and schedule.
dek: The Norwegian runner cited recovery demands after winning Friday’s 5,000 meters during his return from Achilles surgery.
headline: Ingebrigtsen withdraws from 1,500 meters, delaying Kerr showdown
